name: Sao Tome and Principe
headline: Sao Tome and Principe: +1.0% growth in 2025, 0.9% inflation, debt 59% of GDP
sections: Sao Tome and Principe is a $981 million economy (2025), the world's 205th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.0% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $6,388 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 0.6% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 18.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 9.1% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 8.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 59% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 91% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −4.3% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 47% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 10.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 44% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 69.9 years (2024). Population: 240 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
